title: Your Options Trades Just Got a Closer Look: Understanding Derivatives Risk
description: Options are financial contracts giving you the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a set price. India's market regulator, SEBI, is conce.

faq.a: A call option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy an underlying asset at a specific price (strike price) on or before a particular date (expiry date).
A put option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to sell an underlying asset at a specific price (strike price) on or before a particular date (expiry date).
The premium is the price the buyer of an option pays to the seller for the right granted by the option contract. It is the maximum amount an option buyer can lose.

faq.q: Can I lose more than my initial investment (premium) in options?
faq.a: For an option *buyer*, the maximum loss is limited to the premium paid. However, for an option *seller* (also known as an option writer), losses can be significantly higher, potentially unlimited, if the market moves sharply against their position and it's not hedged.

faq.q: Are options trading regulated in India?
faq.a: Yes, options trading in India is regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to ensure market stability and investor protection.
